    Seasonal Poisson surveillance using an earlier baseline

    Source: R/surveillance-seasonal.R
    epi_seasonal_surveillance.Rd

    Fits a Poisson log-linear baseline with Fourier seasonal terms to a separate training data frame, then flags later observed counts that exceed the (1 - alpha) Poisson quantile at the fitted mean. The training observations must all precede the new observations; the model is never fit on the new counts. Fourier period is expressed in the same units as the numeric time column. Optional linear trend is centered and scaled using training time only.

    Usage

    epi_seasonal_surveillance(
  .data,
  time,
  cases,
  training,
  period,
  harmonics = 1L,
  trend = FALSE,
  alpha = 0.05,
  family = c("poisson", "negbin"),
  adjust = "none"
)

    Arguments

    .data

    An ungrouped data frame of later observations to screen.

    time

    A numeric time column, strictly increasing in both datasets.

    cases

    A non-negative integer count column, complete in both datasets.

    training

    An ungrouped data frame of earlier baseline observations with the same time and cases columns.

    period

    Positive length of a seasonal cycle in time units.

    harmonics

    Number of sine/cosine harmonics, between 1 and 5.

    trend

    Whether to include a linear time trend.

    alpha

    Nominal upper-tail probability strictly between zero and one.

    family

    Baseline count model: "poisson" or "negbin".

    adjust

    Multiple-testing adjustment passed to stats::p.adjust(), such as "none", "holm", "bonferroni" or "BH".

    Value

    Input tibble with baseline_expected, threshold (the unadjusted per-row quantile), p_value, p_adjusted and logical alert columns. Counts exactly equal to the threshold are not flagged.

    Details

    The interval threshold is conditional on the fitted mean and ignores parameter uncertainty. Independent Poisson counts, a correctly specified seasonal pattern, a stable exposure/population, and an outbreak-free training period are important assumptions. With family = "negbin" the baseline is a negative binomial model (MASS::glm.nb()), and thresholds and p-values use its estimated dispersion, which reduces false alerts from overdispersed counts. Each row gets an upper-tail p-value P(Y >= cases); with adjust other than "none", alerts use p-values adjusted across all screened rows by stats::p.adjust(), controlling family-wise error or false discovery rate for the batch. Reporting delays, holidays, changing population, baseline outbreaks, trend extrapolation and model selection can still increase false alerts. This is a screening rule, not a validated outbreak detection system; a flag is not an outbreak diagnosis.

    Examples

    train <- data.frame(t = 1:40, cases = rep(c(4, 6, 8, 6), 10))
new <- data.frame(t = 41:42, cases = c(20, 5))
epi_seasonal_surveillance(new, t, cases, training = train, period = 4)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>       t cases baseline_expected threshold      p_value   p_adjusted alert
#>   <int> <dbl>             <dbl>     <dbl>        <dbl>        <dbl> <lgl>
#> 1    41    20              4.17         8 0.0000000197 0.0000000197 TRUE 
#> 2    42     5              5.83        10 0.692        0.692        FALSE
